UPGRADE THE LOCAL AI SUPPORT, deskUnsloth. Design, 2026-10-09. Facts checked at 8924c0dc. Rulings live verbatim in the item they decide.

VISION (Andy's words): the local agent (qwen, on its own node, port 11111) becomes a real party at the desk: it knows what is talked about, its node is "it's sandbox and it's toolset", secured against it, and Andy configures memory, models and agent personas with their tools from a browser. "disregart the ollama agent, i want it to read along for now." And, out of the first item's scope but in the vision by his word: "that agent node should be a puppet of mine, where i can configure it's deskUnsloth remotely, sort of like we do with appFaceApp" and "the permission set may change with every deskUnsloth configuration". And where it goes (his, 2026-10-09): "picture this: a whole goal, designed for one agent persona, with its model configuration paired with it's tool-access-configuration, will tackle the same goal, while i sleep, event descending the dependency tree of that process...." Agents with standing orders, tied to one standing item with its own verification, come after this goal.

THE FOUR ITEMS, IN ANDY'S ORDER
0. API introspection retrofit: every verb declared on both doors (goal/G10.5): the core work, split off 2026-10-09 ("a big enough task for one item, it will require grants for core files"); blocks 1.
1. Endpoint introspection in OpenAI tool shape: the tool list for a key, stripped to its grants at ask time; the agent reads it (his named dependency).
2. The local agent node secured against its agent: out of scope for now by his word of 2026-10-09 (the restriction per persona is its configured tool set; the agent node is expendable while the flow is built); the keyed loopback caller stays the later door change.
3. Context auto-built from the desk goal for the local agent: title, box, last lines and AGENTS go with each line; addressed lines only; one config.
4. Configuration manager: VRAM, models and agent personas: a shell app in three panels; a persona is a configuration on the one agent node with its tool set, chosen from the introspected verbs.

Chain: 0 blocks 1, 1 blocks 2, 2 blocks 4; 3 and 4 block the goal. Every item: a suite red on today's code first; the builder never writes its own tests.

No red Q stands on the goal (2026-10-09): a persona is a configuration with a tool set, not a key and not a node; the Grants app is not involved for the local agent.

[loop.js] To implement this securely and consistently, follow these steps:

### 1. Standardize API Descriptions (OpenAI Compatible)
Ensure all Loopback APIs return JSON schemas matching the **OpenAI Tools** specification (`type: "function"`, `name`, `description`, `parameters`). This allows the UnSloth agent to parse them uniformly.

*   **Action:** Update your Loopback service definitions or middleware to normalize the output before sending it to the agent.

### 2. Implement Source-Based Authentication (Grant System)
Since you control both the browser entry point and the `deskUnsloth` client, you can distinguish users by their **Request Origin** rather than trying to guess intent.

*   **Strategy:** Add a custom header or metadata field in your authentication middleware.
    *   **Humans (Browser):** Set `X-Client-Type: human`.
    *   **Agents (`deskUnsloth`):** Set `X-Client-Type: agent` (or pass this via the token payload).

### 3. Logic Flow for Access Control
Apply a permission matrix based on the identified client type:

| Request Header | Allowed Actions | Rationale |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `X-Client-Type: human` | Read-only, UI-driven actions only. | Prevents accidental data manipulation by users via API calls. |
| `X-Client-Type: agent` | Full read/write access (subject to role-based limits). | Allows UnSloth to execute tools autonomously within its granted scope. |

**Implementation Tip:** In your auth middleware, validate the token signature first, then inspect the attached metadata or header to assign the `agent` vs. `human` flag before evaluating specific API grants.

ENDPOINT INTROSPECTION IN OPENAI TOOL SHAPE: the agent-facing half, refreshed 2026-10-09 to what the retrofit (goal/G10.5) decided. Facts at 512e59d3.

WHAT: deskUnsloth, on the local agent node, builds the standard tool entries from its own node's AGENTS family, which the retrofit provides: AGENTS.introspect lists the verbs that have a file ({items: [{key, label}], more}), AGENTS.<verb> answers that verb's file (its description and, for a loopback verb, its shape by hand), and the generic api answer gives a process server's shapes. From those it makes {type: "function", function: {name, description, parameters}}, parameters a JSON Schema mapped from the prototype ('' string, 0 number, false boolean, [x] array, {} object, every key required), the reply as one extra field, a dotted verb name spelled for a tool name (no dot allowed). Then it hands the model only the verbs the configured task needs (the persona's set, from the configuration manager), never the whole list.

WHY, Andy (2026-10-09): "one dependency i can think of: retrofit the SpiritOS's endpoint introspection to be compatible with the standard tool descriptions for AI agents."; "the permission set may change with every deskUnsloth configuration", so the list is built at ask time, never stored; "so we could use the generic portion of that for the loopback interface, and construct the Open AI compatible version in deskUnsloth?" (yes); "It will be deskUnsloth's job to only provide the agent with the verbs needed for that configured task."

DEPENDS ON: the retrofit (goal/G10.5), decided and design-complete. BLOCKS: The local agent node secured against its agent (goal/G10.2), by his "after that". What a persona may call is that item's; what it is shown is this one's.

TODAY: deskUnsloth sends a bare line to the model with no tools at all; no AGENTS family exists yet (the retrofit builds it).

TESTS FIRST: a suite red on today's code, with a fake AGENTS family: the mapping prototype to JSON Schema, the name spelling, the reply field, the persona set narrowing the list, and that nothing is stored between asks; the builder never writes its own tests.

OUT OF SCOPE here: the model calling a tool and the answer going back (the context item, goal/G10.3), the persona's grants (goal/G10.2), any screen (goal/G10.4).

DECIDED, Andy (2026-10-09): "on the name? it must be unique in a flat file of tools, so the whole bath must be in there, separated by '_' ??" So a tool name is the whole path with underscores, server or namespace first, dots to underscores: desk_item_add, fs_stat; deskUnsloth keeps the table from tool name to {door, verb} it built (Andy: "so deskUnsloth must carry a mapping between Open_AI_Names and a reliable reference to our node and appServer api's?", yes), door being the node itself or a process server by name; built for each model call from the introspection, kept only for that call, never stored; a call the model makes is looked up there and asked of that door as deskEar asks today; nothing is parsed back. And: "no permission prompts to me, every configurations comes with a custom tool set that is pre-approved by virtue of me providing it." So a tool call the model makes runs at once; the pre-approval is the configuration itself. Nothing is left to argue on this item (design-complete pressed 2026-10-09).

items.title: The local agent node secured against its agent
items.box:
THE LOCAL AGENT NODE SECURED AGAINST ITS AGENT, which is puppet-dom: the agent node is the first puppet to use the design strategy decided 2026-10-09, puppet-dom in the core and the features of one puppet in its appServer. Facts at 512e59d3; Andy's words of that day are in this chat.

DECIDED (Andy, 2026-10-09)
1. His own node is protected by the peerPost authentication that exists; what this item protects is the agent's node against the agent itself. The agent node is his puppet (relay-state/owner.json naming him); the owner door takes his signed commands and runs them over the whole node surface, as a loopback client would (the group filter went with cleanup/G1.7).
2. The restriction per persona is its configured tool set, handed to the model by deskUnsloth alone (goal/G10.1, goal/G10.4): a persona is a configuration on the one agent node, not a key and not a node each; the Grants app is not involved for the local agent. The keyed loopback caller is out of scope while the flow is built; the agent node is expendable.
3. Puppet-dom, the same for every puppet and nothing per puppet, three refusals by name on a puppet node: peer.post to a key outside its contacts; the grant verbs (jobs.authGrant, authRevoke, authRelabel), a puppet authorizing nobody to anything, reads of the grants staying; a contact write (contact.accept, block, unblock, label, forget, setSenders) from its own loopback door, contacts being the owner's to write through the owner door. The owner is always among the contacts; desk traffic is unharmed, the desk being the owner's node.
4. A feature of one puppet lives in its appServer: the face's routing to face-owners (who are contacts the owner wrote) and deskUnsloth; the face puppet's features may later move into an appServer, an aside for another goal.

THE HIERARCHY OF ACCESS on the agent node (his, 2026-10-09): first what the node and its servers permit through AGENTS.md and verb files (the retrofit, goal/G10.5); second what the deskUnsloth configuration gives the agent (goal/G10.4 through goal/G10.1); more is out of scope right now.

TODAY: jobs.api hands every loopback caller to the gate as the owner; a member arrives as a verified key and apiDoor refuses what its grant rows do not cover; a puppet node with its own key may peer.post to anyone, grant anything and write its contacts from loopback.

NODE VERB CHANGES: the three refusals touch peer.post, the jobs.auth verbs and the contact verbs; his yes is his rulings of 2026-10-09 in this chat; peer review is owed at build (wsl-claude is signed off; the desk waives alone).

TESTS FIRST: a suite red on today's code with a scratch node whose owner.json names another key: the three refusals, the owner's post and contact write passing, a non-puppet untouched; the builder never writes its own tests.
